## Two Changes to Selective Availability

Selective Availability was a feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. It was stopped in use in May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

That operational change was separate from a later procurement decision. In September 2007, the US government announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability. The announcement did not mark the switch-off of the existing feature; it specified its omission from a future generation, making the 2000 policy durable for GPS III.
